content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides the Matthew 1:16 link by asking whether the passive verb or either text's own words states the contrary, which is the stating-verse approach K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"Phrase: 'When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together'; readings weighed: limited to an already demonstrated chain-vs-chain collision, versus applying here where the judge evaluates the Matthew 1:16 link with the defender's cited verses and asks whether any text's own words state the contrary.","why":"Because K-C retires the stating-verse test and requires chain-against-chain footing, the judge's use of 'neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary' to label the link UNDERDETERMINED breaches the rule."}
